Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: final production image plate for a 600x600 monochrome e-paper Japanese study UI.
Input image is the exact Cutout material composition to preserve. Keep the concrete desk, bright blank paper with torn bottom edge, black paper corner behind, steel paperclip and polished pin. Strict top-down orthographic square, neutral grayscale only.
Change only the lower desk area: add three separate small thick matte charcoal CERAMIC TILE pieces, each nearly rectangular but with imperfect chipped edges, believable cut side faces, tiny scratches and crisp directional shadows. They are real tangible fragments, not app UI buttons. Put the tiles at x=4.5–32%, x=36–63.5%, x=68–95.5%, y=80–93.5%. Similar size and equal emphasis; angles -2, +1, -1 degrees. Leave their upper faces completely blank for legible labels added later in code. Three distinct objects with space between them.
The top 23% must remain clean empty desk for three rows of live weather/calendar text. The central paper is blank for live Japanese text. Preserve the existing central paper shape and position. No text, no Japanese glyphs, no logo, no numbers, no device bezel, no real electronics, no watermark. Reduce the finest desk/paper grain slightly so the light and dark broad shapes remain attractive at 600px and eight grayscale levels. Keep the lovely material realism and sharp paper edges.
